newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Grain use rising among Dutch compounders - Stigevo.
newsitem.headline: Grain use rising among Dutch compounders - Stigevo.

text.p: Grain use by compound feed manufacturers in the Netherlands is continuing to rise steadily and is expected to reach three million tonnes in the 1996/1997 season, market statistician Stigevo said in its latest bulletin.

Grain use touched a low of two million tonnes in the 1992/93 season but has been increasing since then, taking grain's share of the total compound feed mix from 12.5 percent to an expected 19.5 percent this season.
But commercial compounders in the Netherlands still use less grain than those elsewhere in the European Union, largely due to the high volume of available alternatives, Stigevo added.
And because grain prices in the Netherlands were expected to reach their lows for the season at an earlier stage than non-grain feed ingredients, 1997 would see some shift back to grain alternatives.

Stigevo predicted a considerable increase in tapioca use at the expense of grains during the season. It also saw increased use of corn in poultry feed at the expense of wheat and higher wheat use in pig feed at the expense of barley.
It said most of these developments would occur in the first half of 1997 and would "lead to only a limited increase of total grains in compound feed."
